title: Instruct, Not Answer: Using Instruction Privileges in On-Policy Context Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2609.32201v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: On-Policy Context Distillation (OPCD) has recently emerged as a powerful technique for transferring context to student models and for self-improvement. In OPCD, the teacher is conditioned on privileged information, and the goal is to minimize the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the privileged teacher and the student, evaluated on student-generated tokens. Many existing studies show that using instance-specific gold answers or gold demonstrations as the default privilege can hurt training performance, especially out-of-distribution (OOD). In this work, we instead design general instructions that target common student mistakes observed on the training samples, and show that such simple instructions can outperform gold as the OPCD privilege. In autoformalization tasks, using a matched formatting instruction as the privilege could outperform gold in OOD accuracy by a large margin. In 7 out of 8 experiments using ProverQA, ProofW

translated_title: 指示而非作答：在策略上下文蒸馏中使用指令型特权信息
translated_abstract: 在策略上下文蒸馏（OPCD）近来已成为一种强大的技术，可用于向学生模型传递上下文信息以及实现模型自我提升。在OPCD中，教师模型以特权信息为条件，目标是在学生生成的token上最小化特权教师与学生模型之间的Kullback-Leibler（KL）散度。许多现有研究表明，使用针对具体实例的标准答案或标准演示作为默认特权会损害训练性能，尤其是在分布外（OOD）场景下。在这项工作中，我们转而设计了针对训练样本中观察到的学生常见错误的通用指令，并证明这种简单的指令作为OPCD的特权信息可以优于标准答案。在自动形式化任务中，使用匹配的格式指令作为特权信息，在OOD准确率上能够大幅超越标准答案。在使用ProverQA、ProofW的8个实验中有7个……
tldr: 该论文提出在策略上下文蒸馏中，用针对学生常见错误设计的通用指令替代标准答案作为特权信息，可以显著提升训练效果和分布外泛化能力。
en_tdlr: Instead of using gold answers as privileged information in On-Policy Context Distillation, designing simple general instructions that target common student mistakes achieves better training performance and substantially improves out-of-distribution generalization.
